"Would you like help now?"

"Well, it took me a bit to think of the best way to phrase all our questions without having to either lie or disclose any secrets, I hope that got us what we need."

"We talked with Sutri, one of the two of the council who care for a group of shifter children - both to get answers from a prominent member of the community, and someone who took responsibility of caring for the future."

"They definitely value their community a lot - in fact, somewhere through the conversation I realized that what we wrote on the stone here might fit just as well to Feytown by itself. Maybe out of necessity, or maybe out of some greater desire, many races from both this plane and Feywild came together to form one family there. Well, of course, there are... some exceptions we could mention, but that's not the time for them. This is mostly my view, but Feytown seems to be a bit of an idealized miniature of Arcania as a whole - we too, in response to circumstances, band together regardless of our origins."

"But besides the focus on the family, there's another thing quite visible in them - they're determined, they're not giving up. We've learned that the bleeds are a one-way passage, and they haven't had much success in circumventing it, though they're still trying to find a solution. People led by the twins - the Feytown council ones, not the Ravens - fought against the redcoats' iron cage. Even though many can't go back to their home lands, they adapted and keep doing their best for their future."

"Perhaps that's something we can focus on - changes on their own weren't the best idea, but adapting to them, determination, and working for everyone's future."

"As for the place, Cael'fii, the mother-tree, and the park surrounding it, they're important to the borough to warrant that name, but not completely closed off to visitors, would be my first guess. After that, the hilltops where the children - the future - live."
